risk_if_not_implemented: Without Limiting Personal Data (PD) Disclosures, Personal Data (PD) may be collected, processed, retained or shared without lawful authority or adequate safeguards, harming individuals and exposing the organization to regulatory action. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unauthorized Access (R-AC-4), Regulatory / Legal / Contractual Financial Liability (R-EX-5), Loss of Confidentiality (R-IP-2), Privacy Harm / Unauthorized Processing (R-IP-6), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Statutory / Regulatory / Contractual Change (MT-11).

compensating_control_1.name: Data Privacy Program
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation and operation of data protection controls throughout the data lifecycle to ensure all forms of Personal Data (PD) are processed lawfully, fairly and transparently.
compensating_control_1.justification: Data Privacy Program (PRI-02) provides policy-level governance that compensates for the absence of Limiting Personal Data (PD) Disclosures (PRI-01.7) by establishing documented expectations, accountability structures, and organizational guardrails. Given the data-handling focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Statutory, Regulatory & Contractual Compliance
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the identification and implementation of relevant statutory, regulatory and contractual controls.
compensating_control_2.justification: Statutory, Regulatory & Contractual Compliance (CPL-02) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Limiting Personal Data (PD) Disclosures (PRI-01.7) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Data applicability. Given the data-handling focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
